parts.text: Describe the case study as a research method.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design an alternative way to investigate REM and dreaming using the case study method
and describe how it could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Evaluate this alternative way of studying REM and dreaming in methodological and practical
terms.

text: Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreaming) carried out a laboratory experiment to investigate the
relationship between REM sleep and dreaming. An alternative way to investigate dreaming would
be to carry out a case study.

parts.text: What is meant by the term ‘quantitative data’?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one quantitative finding from the study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of collecting quantitative data using the Tajfel study as
an example.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the extent to which the findings of Tajfel’s study can be applied to everyday life. 
Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Tajfel conducted a study to investigate intergroup categorisation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘reductionism’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test)
Bandura et al. (aggression)
Maguire et al. (taxi drivers)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What problems may psychologists have when they carry out reductionist research?

parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the ‘cognitive approach’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Loftus and Pickrell (false memories)
Held and Hein (kitten carousel)
Mann et al. (lying)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the cognitive processes investigated in each of these studies.

parts.text:
What advantages may psychologists have when they investigate cognitive processes?
